analysis.title: Bond markets
key_insights: October saw corporate bond spreads widen across the board. Flight-to-quality and lower benchmark yields kept IG total returns positive, while HY is likely to end the month negative.

Spread widening was driven by spiking government bond yields and elevated rates volatility early in the month, then by concerns over the scale, financing and returns of AI investment that hit tech stocks and broader risk assets.

European credit underperformed the US in both IG and HY after fiscal concerns and political unrest in France widened the OAT-Bund spread. EUR HY returns remain deeply negative given lower duration and larger spread widening. Real estate and CCC credit also lagged.

UBS sees value in credit after the cheapening in October, with all-in yields near historical highs. Fundamentals are resilient, liquidity is adequate and many IG borrowers have well-termed-out maturities. Gross issuance could accelerate in November as reporting blackouts end.

Core preference is intermediate-maturity bonds of A and BBB rated borrowers, especially utilities, telecoms and energy, plus select industrials and systemically important banks. Highlighted names are ABB, Barclays, BAWAG, EssilorLuxottica, Union Pacific and Netflix.
In higher-beta credit, UBS favors the stronger end of the quality range: Carnival, Levi Strauss, Telecom Italia and Silgan. Select hybrids from high-quality IG issuers are also favored.

Near-term risks are rate volatility, French politics ahead of the April elections, and hyperscaler earnings and capex and financing plans. UBS economists do not expect the rate hikes currently priced by markets to fully materialize.

Recommendation changes on 28 Oct: Carnival added to Preferred, Tesco added to Core, Goldman Sachs and Bank of America moved from Preferred to Core. Albertsons outlook cut to Deteriorating from Stable, United Rentals outlook moved to Stable from Improving.

US Big 6 banks 3Q26: markets revenue rose 16% y/y with equities up 43% and FICC down 4%. Investment banking revenue rose 8%. Asset quality is resilient. UBS sees capital consumption, not credit losses, as the key credit risk.

CET1 fell 30bps to 13.9% at JPM, 30bps to 10.9% at BAC and 50bps to 12.4% at GS. GS warrants the closest monitoring, with a roughly 50bps SLR buffer versus 100-200bps at peers and financing-led balance-sheet growth.

GS moved to Core because balance-sheet growth and heavy senior funding supply limit its outperformance to the carry advantage. BAC moved to Core because its spreads are only modestly wider than JPM's and give limited compensation for the governance headline.
BAC recorded a USD1.2bn AML charge and consent order. S&P upgraded WFC's HoldCo rating to A- from BBB+. UBS keeps MS on Preferred and JPM, Citi and WFC on Core.
Albertsons withdrew FY26 guidance pending a business review. UBS puts leverage at 4.3x against S&P's 4.0x downgrade threshold for a second quarter, and views the bonds as fairly valued.

Carnival returned to Preferred as fuel-cost concerns look overdone. Net leverage is 3.2x, the target is 2.75x by 2029, and UBS sees up to 60bps of spread tightening toward BBB levels and the Royal Caribbean discount.

EQT's all-equity acquisition of Range Resources is credit positive. UBS expects a one-notch upgrade at Moody's and S&P on closing and 5-10bps of spread compression versus peers. Weak gas prices and a warm winter are risks.
Schneider Electric's USD23.7bn PTC acquisition lifts leverage temporarily (EUR16-17bn new debt against EUR15.4bn net debt). UBS sees tightening potential in select bonds after the spread widening.
Silgan's Trivium combination keeps consolidated net leverage at about 3.4x, and S&P and Moody's put ratings on watch negative. UBS views the spread widening as an opportunity.
Telecom Italia was upgraded by Moody's to Baa3 with a positive outlook. UBS expects S&P to follow into IG. Much of the improvement is priced in, but select bonds still offer value and carry.
United Rentals beat 3Q26 with revenue up 15.7% to USD4.9bn, 3.9% above consensus, and raised FY26 guidance for the third time. It is now IG at both agencies and UBS sees the bonds as fairly valued.
Volvo Car's 3Q26 results disappointed: revenue fell 23% y/y, adjusted EBIT was a SEK3.7bn loss, and a one-notch downgrade is now probable. Outlook stays Deteriorating.

Skydance, formed on 6 Oct, has pro forma net debt of about USD83bn, or roughly 6.9x leverage. Spreads range from about 165bps on IG first-lien notes to over 600bps on legacy unsecured debt. UBS expects wide spreads to persist.
Moody's affirmed France at Aa3 with a negative outlook on 23 Oct. UBS keeps Deteriorating outlooks on SocGen, Ayvens and BFCM and cautions against outsized French bank exposure.
Webuild's headline EUR22bn of reserves overstates its exposure. UBS sees tightening in the longer end, subject to a supportive HY market. Short bonds through 2029 have already retraced the move.

Other updates: Netflix cut FY26 revenue guidance to about USD51.1bn on slower ad growth but credit is unaffected. Union Pacific's USD85bn Norfolk Southern deal has a key date on 18 Nov. Campbell's and Pernod Ricard debuted hybrids and both stay Deteriorating.

market_movers.rationale: Carnival added to the Preferred list. UBS expects up to 60bps of spread tightening as credit metrics improve and the discount to Royal Caribbean narrows.

sector_views.rationale: Defensive sectors favored within intermediate-maturity A and BBB rated bonds.
Strong asset quality and NII support, but capital consumption is rising. GS and BAC were cut from Preferred to Core.
UBS cautions against outsized French bank bond exposure given the sovereign backdrop and possible Moody's downgrade of France.
